facts.fact_text: The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk held that the organiser of the gathering at the Art School should have notified the regional authorities of the meeting.

The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk found the first applicant guilty of participation in an unauthorised public event, an offence under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk sentenced the first applicant to a fine of 500 Russian roubles (RUB).

The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk held that the second applicant had organised a public event, namely a gathering of ten participants, without notifying the regional authorities.

The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk held that the third applicant had organised a public event, namely a gathering of ten participants, without notifying the regional authorities.

The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk found the second applicant guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced the second applicant to a fine of RUB 2,000.

The justice of the peace of the 81st judicial circuit of the Central District of Novorossiysk found the third applicant guilty under Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences and sentenced the third applicant to a fine of RUB 2,000.

The Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk upheld the first-instance court's finding that the gathering on 23 January 2007 had been a public event subject to the requirement of notification of the authorities.

Article 20.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, as in force at the material time, provided that breaches of the established procedure for the organisation of public gatherings, meetings, demonstrations, marches or pickets shall be punishable by an administrative fine of between ten and twenty times the minimum wage, for the organisers.

Article 20.2 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001, as in force at the material time, provided that breaches of the established procedure for the conduct of public gatherings, meetings, demonstrations, marches or pickets shall be punishable by an administrative fine of, for the organisers, between ten and twenty times the minimum wage, and, for the participants, between five and ten times the minimum wage.

Section 7 of the Public Events Act provided that notification of a public event (except for a gathering and a picket held by a solo participant) must be filed in writing by its organiser with the executive or municipal authority no earlier than fifteen days and no later than ten days before the date of the public event.

Section 8(1) of the Public Events Act provided that a public event may be held in any convenient location, provided that it does not create a risk of building collapse or any other risks to the safety of the participants, and that the access of participants to certain locations may be banned or restricted in the circumstances specified by federal laws.

The officials from the Department of Culture and the Department of Cooperation with Public Organisations and Monitoring of Migration of Novorossiysk requested the participants to leave the meeting room on the grounds that no notification of a public event had been sent to the Department of Culture.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk found that, in accordance with the local administration's directives and in order to combat terrorism, schools had to notify any planned events.
The members of FRODO refused to give any explanation to the police officers on the grounds that no charges had been brought against them.
The meeting participants refused to leave the meeting room on the grounds that their meeting was not public and therefore did not require notification.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk found that the police had acted lawfully and within their powers in order to verify a report of an unauthorised entry onto the Art School's premises.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk found that the applicants had not been arrested or removed from the Art School's premises during the police check on 23 January 2007.
The Oktyabrskiy District Court of Novorossiysk found that the applicants could have continued their meeting elsewhere after the police check on 23 January 2007.
